passage: Monday: Himani held out a spoonful of soup and Pallavi, two, shook her head firmly from side to side, lips shut. Himani put the spoon down. Wednesday: a visitor offered a plastic toy and Pallavi shook her head and hid behind the sofa, so Himani thanked the visitor and said Pallavi would look later. Friday: Himani held up two pairs of shoes. Pallavi shook her head at the blue ones and pointed at the red. “Red it is,” said Himani.

qa.q: Which pair of shoes did Pallavi choose on Friday?
qa.a: The red ones, which she pointed at after shaking her head at the blue.

qa.q: What was Pallavi probably feeling each time she shook her head?
qa.a: With the soup and the toy she was probably unwilling or uneasy, since she shut her lips and hid behind the sofa, while on Friday she seemed pleased to choose the red shoes. She may also have enjoyed feeling in charge.

qa.q: What made Himani's responses helpful?
qa.a: She respected the refusal without a fight and gave a choice on Friday, which let Pallavi say what she wanted.

qa.q: How might the visitor feel when Pallavi shakes her head?
qa.a: The visitor may feel a little awkward, but Himani's thanks shows it is not personal.

grounding: A toddler shakes her head to refuse before she can speak clearly, and an adult responds with respect.

passage: Wasim peeled a banana in the flat's small kitchen and held it towards Devika's high chair. She shook her head, once each way, then again, lips pressed tight, eyes on his face. “No banana?” he said. She shook her head again. “Okay. Apple?” Devika looked at the apple bowl and nodded so hard her curls bounced. Wasim laughed, cut a slice and gave it to her. She ate it, happily swinging her legs.

qa.q: What did Devika refuse in the kitchen?
qa.a: The banana that Wasim peeled.

qa.q: What was Devika probably feeling when she shook her head at the banana?
qa.a: She was probably reluctant to eat the banana and keen to have a say, since she pressed her lips tight and then nodded hard for apple. She might also have been full or simply wanted something different.

qa.q: What could Wasim try if she refuses the apple too?
qa.a: He could stay calm, put the food away and offer again later without pressure.

qa.q: How might Wasim feel when she says no with her head?
qa.a: He may be a little amused and proud that she can already let him know her mind. 😊

grounding: A toddler shakes her head to say no and show her wish for control, and an adult responds with respect.

passage:
"Siddharth, sweater on, it's cold."
Siddharth shook his head hard, side to side, and clutched his arms to his chest.
"He's just being difficult," said his father.
"He's telling us no," said Jaya, his mother. "Sid, no sweater?"
Another hard shake.
"Okay. Red jacket or blue jacket?"
He stopped shaking, looked at both, and patted the blue one.
"Blue it is," Jaya said, and he pushed his own arm into the sleeve.

qa.q: Which jacket did Siddharth choose?
qa.a: He patted the blue one.

qa.q: What did Siddharth's hard head shake and clutched arms suggest he wanted?
qa.a: He was refusing the sweater and wanted some say over what he wore; once he got a choice he calmed and seemed satisfied, pushing his own arm into the sleeve.

qa.q: Which choice of Jaya's worked, and why?
qa.a: Treating the head shake as a real "no" and offering two jackets worked, because Siddharth kept some control while still getting warm.

qa.q: How does Siddharth's father read the head shake?
qa.a: He sees it as being difficult, rather than as Siddharth's way of saying no before he has the words.

grounding: A toddler shakes his head to refuse, and his mother responds with respect by offering a choice.

passage: Daycare note, Tuesday. When I carried Mridul to the sandpit this morning, he shook his head over and over and turned his body back toward the room. I put him down and said, "No sand today. Okay." I didn't insist. I sat him near the water tray instead, where he watched for a while and then poured water from cup to cup for a long time. His "no" was clear, and he stayed calm once it was heard. Pradeep, daycare teacher

qa.q: Where did Mridul play instead of the sandpit?
qa.a: At the water tray, pouring water from cup to cup.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling when he shook his head at the sandpit?
qa.a: He was likely uneasy or simply did not want the sand, and he was saying so clearly; once his "no" was heard he stayed calm and content.

qa.q: What would you advise other staff who work with Mridul?
qa.a: Take his head shake as a real answer, offer another activity and don't force him, as Pradeep did.

qa.q: How might Mridul's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They would probably feel glad that his "no" was respected and that he still had a happy morning.

grounding: A daycare teacher treats a toddler's head shake as meaningful refusal and responds with respect.

passage:
At the village gurdwara langar, Kalyani, a neighbour, held out a round ladoo to little Jasleen. Jasleen shook her head and pressed her face into her mother's arm.
"Take it, beta, don't be rude," her mother whispered.
Jasleen shook her head again, harder.
Kalyani smiled and lowered her hand. "She's said no. That's fine." Jasleen peeked at her. A minute later she reached out for a piece of roti instead.

qa.q: What did Kalyani offer Jasleen?
qa.a: A round ladoo.

qa.q: What did Jasleen's harder head shake show?
qa.a: She was firmly refusing and perhaps a bit shy of Kalyani; when her "no" was accepted she seemed more at ease, peeking and reaching for roti.

qa.q: What could Jasleen's mother try next time?
qa.a: She could accept the head shake as a polite enough "no" at this age, instead of pushing her to take food.

qa.q: How does Jasleen's mother see the head shake?
qa.a: She worries it looks rude to the neighbour, while Kalyani sees a clear and fair "no".

grounding: A toddler shakes her head to refuse food, and a neighbour accepts it as real communication.

passage:
A grey morning in Valencia. Rafael held up the thick red coat. “Coat on, Rosa, it's cold.”
Rosa shook her head hard, side to side, and backed against the fridge.
Rafael didn't grab her arm. He crouched. “No coat? Okay. Coat or jumper?” He held up both.
Rosa looked from one to the other, then pointed at the striped jumper and lifted her arms.
“Jumper it is,” said Rafael, and they were out of the door.

qa.q: What did Rosa back up against?
qa.a: She backed against the fridge.

qa.q: What was Rosa feeling when she shook her head at the coat?
qa.a: She was feeling cross and determined to refuse the coat, and probably wanted some control over what she wore; a head shake is her way of saying no before she has many words.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Rafael treated the head shake as real communication and offered a choice between two warm things, which respected her no and still got her dressed.

qa.q: How did Rafael feel when Rosa shook her head, judging by what he did?
qa.a: He seems patient rather than annoyed, since he crouched calmly instead of grabbing her arm.

grounding: It shows a toddler shaking her head to refuse, showing a wish for control, and a parent responding to it with respect.
